F_codex_round2_consultation.verdict_summary: Codex round-2 says mostly shippable via unit+typecheck but flags 9 concrete BA-ticket improvements to fold into dev TODO. findings.claim: runStartupSweep starts runSweepInline(state) BEFORE enqueueing it (codexMappingDaemon.ts:120-123). Sweep can race with concurrent queued upserts/removes; atomicWriteJson tmp suffix .<pid> collides on same-process concurrent writes.
findings.qa_assessment: Valid concern but PRE-EXISTING behavior — not introduced by M1'. Note pattern: `const p = runSweepInline(state); enqueue(state, () => p); return p;` — the enqueued task awaits the already-running promise, not a fresh invocation, so the second writer only completes after the first resolves. Recommend BA flag this as observation rather than block landing — it's existing infra, M1' merely reads sweep.removed return value.

findings.claim: AC2 says 'counter increments' but field name and BA hint say 'last' (set semantics).
findings.qa_assessment: Terminology clarification. Field name 'lastSweepRemoved' = set semantics (value of most-recent sweep). Recommend AC2 rephrasing: 'lastSweepRemoved reflects sweep.removed return value' — set, not increment.

findings.claim: readCgroupForPid(pid) hardcoding /proc/<pid>/cgroup not unit-testable on non-Linux (vitest may run on macOS dev). Need pure parser parseCgroupRaw(raw, readAt) exported separately.
findings.qa_assessment: Valid. CI runs on Linux but vitest dev loop may be cross-platform. Recommend dev extract pure parser parseCgroupRaw separately + readCgroupForPid as thin wrapper. AC4 should explicitly require the pure parser export for testability.

findings.claim: queueUpsert only truthy-checks pid; M3 now passes pid into fs path. Should Number.isInteger + pid > 0 guard before reading /proc/<pid>/cgroup.
findings.qa_assessment: Valid defensive hardening. Already implicit (TS types say pid: number) but runtime metadata is z.any per controlServer. Recommend dev adds the guard inside readCgroupForPid.

findings.claim: isValidEntry doesn't validate cgroup; malformed persisted cgroup returned as trusted. Add isValidCgroupInfo or strip on read.
findings.qa_assessment: Valid for defense-in-depth. M3' new field deserves a validator. Recommend dev adds isValidCgroupInfo helper called inside isValidEntry.

findings.topic: AC4 merge ambiguity (fresh vs preserve existing)
findings.claim: BA says mergeEntry 'prefer fresh else existing'; AC says non-Linux omits. Ambiguous for re-upsert where prior had valid cgroup and current read fails.
findings.qa_assessment: Recommend explicit BA rule: 'New entry with unreadable cgroup → field omitted. Existing entry with valid cgroup re-upserted with unreadable cgroup → PRESERVE existing cgroup (do not overwrite with undefined).' Dev should encode in mergeEntry.

findings.claim: resumeExistingThread.test.ts already exercises helper via mocked controlClient; M2' will leak process.title state across suites. Need afterEach restore in resume tests too, not only helper test.
findings.qa_assessment: Valid. Recommend dev adds afterEach('restore original process.title') in BOTH notifyDaemonOfCodexTid.test.ts AND resumeExistingThread.test.ts. Avoid skipProcessTitle production flag — keep production path clean.

findings.claim: Helper unit test + resume unit test + static grep evidence that runCodex.ts:712 still calls helper is sufficient under unit-only QA. Don't require live runCodex integration.
findings.qa_assessment: Agreed. AC3 already accepts this — start-path coverage is via centralization through the helper.

observations_for_ba_or_dev.observation: Codex round-2 #1 — runStartupSweep race-with-chain pattern is PRE-EXISTING. M1' does not introduce it. Dev should confirm via reading runStartupSweep that `const p = runSweepInline(state); enqueue(state, () => p); return p;` enqueues the same already-running promise (so chain serialization holds), not a fresh sweep invocation. If chain semantics break, surface as observation; otherwise no action needed.

Codex round-2 #2 — AC2 says 'counter increments' but technical hint says 'set state.lastSweepRemoved = sweep.removed'. Field name 'lastSweepRemoved' (last, singular) supports set semantics. Recommend BA edit AC2 to: 'lastSweepRemoved reflects the most recent sweep.removed value (set on each sweep, not cumulative).' Dev should test both first-sweep (removed > 0) and second-sweep (removed = 0) cases to confirm set-not-accumulate behavior.

Codex round-2 #3 — For AC4 unit-testability across platforms, dev should extract `parseCgroupRaw(raw: string, readAt: string): CgroupInfo` as a pure exported function in codexMapping.ts (or sibling), with `readCgroupForPid(pid)` being a thin Linux-only wrapper that reads /proc/<pid>/cgroup and calls parseCgroupRaw. Unit tests target parseCgroupRaw with v1/v2/mixed/unknown fixture strings; integration test exercises readCgroupForPid against process.pid on Linux CI.

Codex round-2 #4 + #5 — Defensive validation: (a) inside readCgroupForPid, guard `if (!Number.isInteger(pid) || pid <= 0) return undefined;` before fs read; (b) add `isValidCgroupInfo(c)` helper used inside isValidEntry to strip malformed persisted cgroup data. Both are minor hardening, fold into M3' implementation.

Codex round-2 #6 — AC4 should disambiguate cgroup merge on re-upsert: 'New entry with unreadable cgroup → cgroup field omitted. Existing entry re-upserted with unreadable cgroup → PRESERVE existing cgroup (do not overwrite with undefined).' Recommend BA edits AC4 OR Technical Hints M3' to encode this rule in mergeEntry.

Codex round-2 #7 — process.title test leakage: dev must add `afterEach(() => { process.title = original; })` in BOTH notifyDaemonOfCodexTid.test.ts AND resumeExistingThread.test.ts (the resume test already calls the real helper through a mocked controlClient). Avoid production `skipProcessTitle` flag — keep production-path code clean.

Codex round-2 #9 — In M4' roadmap doc, mirror BA's exact M1' phrasing ('mapping-health telemetry, NOT a replacement for the bash-side fd-scan fallback counter from Block 3') so M1' and M4' are terminology-consistent and reviewers don't conflate the two counters.
